contracts: D1 module shape: new vendor/truck/truck-shapeops/src/section.rs opens with the house deny header (recognize.rs:22-29); lib.rs declares `pub mod section;` (A1 2->3, A4 0->1); new vendor/truck/truck-shapeops/tests/split_plane.rs carries the same deny header plus a match-based `fn expect_ok<T>(r: Outcome<T>) -> T`.

D2 over-box: private `solid_over_box(&Solid<Point3, Curve, Surface>) -> Outcome<((f64,f64),(f64,f64),(f64,f64))>`; per-face carrier table reimplemented locally (no truck-modeling edge): Plane/Cylinder faces hull the boundary edges' `EnclosureCurve::enclose` boxes over each edge's own range; Sphere faces take the full `[c-r, c+r]^3` carrier box; Cone faces take the edge boxes plus the apex; Torus / `CanonicalSurface::Placed` / Unrecognized refuse `UnsupportedEnvelope(NonCanonicalCarrier)` BEFORE any Boolean is paid for. Stored wires via `Face::absolute_boundaries()`.

D3 halfspace boxes: `halfspace_box` builds the axis-aligned pad-box (over-box extended by `pad = 2 * max over-box dimension` on every side) clipped by the closed halfspace of the cutting plane, as a convex polyhedron through 8-vertex/12-edge/6-face hexahedron topology where the cut allows, `Solid::try_new` as the gate. The wall face lies exactly IN Pi and carries the caller's `Plane` value (crossings taken exactly at the plane origin's coordinate for axis-aligned planes), so cap identification is exact-equality. Adjacent faces share one `Edge` instance per vertex-index pair.

D4 split: `pub fn split_by_plane(&Solid, &Plane, &mut Budget) -> Outcome<(Solid, Solid)>` = `boolean(S, Difference, minus_box)` for `plus` (the side the normal points to) and `boolean(S, Intersection, minus_box)` for `minus`; the composed spend is reported via `Certificate::accumulate`. `pub fn section_faces(&Solid, &Plane, &mut Budget) -> Outcome<Vec<Face>>` runs the Difference half and extracts the faces whose `Surface::Plane` data equals the wall's `Plane` exactly (C0, no tolerance).

D5 v1 envelope: no pre-screening and no new refusal arms; non-canonical faces refuse at the over-box lift, the oblique-cylinder RW-CONIC refusal surfaces from inside `boolean()`, and coplanar/unrecognized carriers answer exactly what the landed pipeline answers.
D6 certificates: both operations certify through the landed `Solid::try_new` acceptance gate; `section_faces` additionally certifies cap extraction by exact plane identity (a lookup, not a solve).

Test battery: 10 dyadic-witness tests in tests/split_plane.rs (all green): split_flagship_plate_through_middle, split_recombination_is_original, split_box_diagonal_plane, section_faces_of_plate, section_face_with_hole_annulus, plane_missing_returns_whole_plus_empty, oblique_cylinder_section_refuses, sphere_face_refuses_noncanonical, split_signs_follow_normal, halves_survive_further_boolean.

deviations.deviation: Test 7 (oblique_cylinder_section_refuses) asserts the machine-checked arm `Refusal::NumericallyUnresolved { witness: UncertifiedContainment, .. }`, not `ContactReductionDeferred`.
deviations.derivation: The oblique plane x z-aligned cylinder wall is the booked RW-CONIC boundary; D5 says the typed refusal the caller sees is the landed one (do not pre-screen, do not catch). This run's landed arm is the splitter's failed insertion projection (`numerically_unresolved`, UncertifiedContainment), so that is the assertion.

The diagonal cut (x + y = 2 through the 2x2x2 box's opposite edges) is the booked vertex-touch cut boundary (deferred list, session 41; amendment r2 re-books it as a boundary assertion). The packet records the class across three instrumented stops as ContactReductionDeferred / NumericallyUnresolved(UncertifiedContainment); this run's landed arm (verified by a scratch harness against the committed code) is ContactReductionDeferred. The test asserts the OR of the two recorded classes with the mandated boundary comment.

deviations.deviation: Test 10's `small_box` is `truck_modeling::primitive::cuboid` at dyadic coordinates ([1.5,2.5]^2 x [0.5,2.5]) instead of an extruded `box_profile` box.
deviations.derivation: An extruded box sharing a face plane with a half (e.g. a [0,1]^2 x [0,2] box under/over the plate) produces a coplanar partial-overlap contact pair that the landed pipeline refuses with UnsupportedEnvelope(ContactReductionDeferred) - the landed partial-overlap family boundary, not a packet stop (test 10 is outside the amendment's stop set {1,2,4,5,6}). The cuboid sits on dyadic coordinates off every half's face plane, so each half is consumed by a REAL transverse Difference cut and both results are valid single-shell solids.

deviations.deviation: D3's `plus_box` is not separately emitted; only `minus_box` is constructed.
deviations.derivation: D4's exact recipes compose both boolean() calls against the negative halfspace box only (Difference and Intersection both use minus_box), so a separate plus_box solid is dead code. The halfspace-box helper is sign-parameterized (the `negative` flag) and covers the mirror construction on the positive side, so the plus_box capability is present but unexercised.
